Hard gate per WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 2d and .claude/agents/reviewer.md's own procedure (idiomatic-vs-crutch, supervision integrity N/A here — no process/supervisor touched, type-safety gaps, scope creep) plus docs/anti-patterns.md. 1. DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY CHECK (explicitly asked for by REQ-358's own requirement text, quoted above): read docs/migration/decisions/0004-humanless-pipeline.md's 'What is explicitly NOT reproduced' section and confirm the reading this run has proceeded on — that Decision 0004's deferral of R-Co's BO-*/PRODUCT-OWNER persona layer was conditioned on 'when S7 actually starts and there is a concrete scenario corpus to validate against', and that REQ-210 (done) already confirmed both preconditions are met — is correct, i.e. this run is not silently re-deciding a settled decision but is executing its already-stated trigger condition. State this confirmation (or disagreement) explicitly in your result; do not silently pass over it.

2. THE MIX_ENV COMPILE-WARNING FINDING ELIXIR-DEV FLAGGED (see handoffs/WF02-REQ358-20260916/step-02a-elixir-dev.json's result.issues, in artifacts_in): lib/mix/tasks/ compiles under every Mix env, and a bare `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` with no MIX_ENV set warns because YamlElixir is scoped `only: :test` in mix.exs's deps(). Confirmed non-blocking for THIS project's actual CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml runs only `mix letflow.check`, which is forced to :test via mix.exs's preferred_envs — verify this yourself, don't take it on faith) and for GIT_MERGE.md Step Final's own gate sequence (also runs under whatever env the alias/task forces). Judge: is this an acceptable, documented tradeoff (leave yaml_elixir `only: :test`, since every actual gate this project runs already forces :test) or a genuine idiom/robustness gap that should be fixed now (e.g. widen yaml_elixir's dep scope to remove the env-dependency footgun entirely for any future bare `mix compile` invocation, interactive dev session, or editor tooling)? Either verdict is acceptable — PASS with a recorded non-blocking note, or FAIL with a specific required fix — but it must be a reasoned call, not silently dropped.

Standard checks: read the diff (git diff main...HEAD), verify the new mix task follows the check_requirements_registration precedent idiomatically (pure core / thin Mix.Task wrapper), verify no scope creep beyond REQ-358's SCOPE section (no new agent role, no permanent scenario content beyond the throwaway fixture, no visual-regression code), verify the throwaway fixture is clearly marked as such and not silently promoted to permanent corpus.

result.summary:
JUDGMENT CALL 1 (Decision 0004 consistency) -- CONFIRMED, no re-decision. Read 0004's 'What is explicitly NOT reproduced' section directly: it defers the BO-*/PRODUCT-OWNER persona layer 'to when S7 actually starts and there is a concrete scenario corpus to validate against.' Read REQ-210 (done) directly in docs/requirements.yaml: it states S7 is done and the corpus exists (11 tenant scenarios/3 companies, 18 platform scenarios). Both trigger preconditions are genuinely met, not asserted on faith. Also confirmed REQ-358 itself stays inside 0004's still-standing boundary -- its own SCOPE excludes 'no new agent role'; the actual persona-role work (0004's specific deferred item) is REQ-359 (BA role, pending) and REQ-361 (PO-equivalent, pending), not this requirement. This is the deferred work's trigger firing, not 0004's reasoning being reopened.

JUDGMENT CALL 2 (MIX_ENV/yaml_elixir) -- FAIL, required fix, not a documented tradeoff. Verified myself rather than trusting the handoff's framing: mix.exs's preferred_envs only forces :test for the `letflow.check` alias. Read docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md step 5d directly (the conflict-handling 'verify the build still passes' block) -- it runs a bare `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, NOT via the alias, so it is NOT forced to :test; ORCH's framing in this handoff's own task text ('GIT_MERGE.md Step Final's own gate sequence also runs under whatever env the alias/task forces') is incorrect for this step. This step is real and currently active (used repeatedly per docs/anti-patterns.md's own entries on this exact gate), triggered on any future rebase conflict, which will occur on some future branch regardless of what that branch touches, since lib/ always compiles. anti-patterns.md's 'elixirc --warnings-as-errors is not a proxy for mix compile --warnings-as-errors' entry underscores how precisely this project already treats this exact gate's exit-code behavior -- a spurious warning here would be read by a rebase-resolving agent as 'fix compile errors, git add, rebase --continue,' i.e. a false-positive bug hunt, exactly the kind of reliability gap the humanless-pipeline redundancy principle exists to close. REQUIRED FIX: widen yaml_elixir's dep scope in mix.exs from `only: :test` to `only: [:dev, :test]` -- a one-line, zero-risk change that removes the env-dependency footgun entirely rather than leaving it as documented debt. Route to ELIXIR-DEV.

STANDARD CHECKS: lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_uat_scenario_schema.ex read in full -- correctly follows check_requirements_registration's precedent (pure check_scenario/2 core, never raises on malformed content; thin run/1 Mix.Task wrapper; @spec on every public/private boundary function). Supervision N/A, confirmed no process/supervisor file touched (git diff --stat). Branching construct is exactly eq/in/else, no general expression language -- matches REQ-358's own scope limit. Throwaway fixture (test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/_throwaway/login-routing-example.yaml) is clearly marked disposable in its own header comment and lives under a `_throwaway/` directory, not silently promoted to permanent corpus. No new agent role, no visual-regression code -- confirmed via diff --stat (18 files, all doc/handoff/fixture/mix-task, no new behaviour/role file). docs/anti-patterns.md checked: no direct-precedent entry for dep `only:` scoping, but the 'elixirc vs mix compile --warnings-as-errors' entry (line 1339) and the 'test-only production-code seam' entry (line 2199) both reinforce this project's low tolerance for MIX_ENV-dependent gate surprises, supporting the FAIL-with-fix call above rather than the PASS-with-note alternative.

MINOR non-blocking note: .claude/agents/uat-runner.md's and WF-05_uat_run.md's updated 'Note on scope' sections read 'As of REQ-361, Letflow has that equivalent role' in present tense, but REQ-361 is status: pending (not done) -- the wording technically uses the requested 'as of REQ-361' citation form but its present-tense grammar ('has') reads as already-landed rather than conditional-on-landing, which is the exact confusion REQ-358's own task text warned against ('do not forward-reference an agent that does not exist yet as though it already does'). Not blocking this gate (no functional/code impact, and the literal citation is present), but flag for DOC-UPDATER/next touch to reword as conditional (e.g. 'once REQ-361 lands, Letflow will have...').
